newsitem.title: CANADA: Pools ask regulators to scrap poison pill.
newsitem.headline: Pools ask regulators to scrap poison pill.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators on Friday asked regulators to prohibit United Grain Growers Ltd's shareholder rights plan now that they have dropped their hostile takeover bid for UGG, AWP chief financial officer Geoff Southwood said.

"We want to cease trading of the shareholder rights plan, that's separate from the poison pill. We've got an axe over our head for as long as they've got this plan so we'd like the plan cease-traded," Southwood said in a phone interview.
Directors of UGG Thursday indefinitely postponed the implementation of its shareholder rights plan.
UGG shares traded down C$0.15 at C$12.60 at 1123 EST on the Toronto Stock Exchange with 13,522 shares changing hands.
"United Grain Growers have the right to issue those rights and we don't like that because it's a hammer over our heads," Southwood said.
AWP and MPE applied to securities commissions in Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba and Ontario for the cease order, he said.
Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators on February 20 launched a C$13.75 a share hostile bid for UGG, one of Canada's largest grain handlers.
They dropped their C$172 million offer Tuesday after a Manitoba court ruled UGG's poison pill had been triggered.

UGG's directors adopted the poison pill on February 14. It grants any shareholder other than a hostile bidder the option to purchase 8.5 more shares for each one already held at C$5.88 each. The plan could be triggered once any one shareholder acquired 15 percent or more of UGG's stock.
